official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR Ground Truth Surveys — independent elevation checkpoints
official_sources.finding: The archive contains independently surveyed elevation points used to verify EA timestamped LIDAR. Ground-truth points are reported at +/-3 cm RMSE and include survey date, surface type, survey method, transformation and geoidal-model attribution; LIDAR QC compares RMSE, standard deviation and random error.
official_sources.limitation: The public catalogue does not provide the specific residual result for every LIDAR survey; target-parcel use requires binding the parcel's contributing survey to its own ground-truth result or fail closed.
official_sources.licence_or_attribution: Open Government Licence; Environment Agency attribution stated on dataset page

official_sources.title: Defra Survey Data Catalogue FAQ — LiDAR vertical accuracy
official_sources.finding: EA specifications require absolute height RMSE below +/-15 cm and expect relative/random height error no more than +/-5 cm; the FAQ directs users to survey-specific ground-truth results.
official_sources.limitation: These are programme acceptance thresholds, not measured uncertainty for a specific parcel or a specific pair of extrema.
official_sources.licence_or_attribution: Environment Agency/Defra public support page; captured excerpt does not separately assert a licence

official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m — national metadata and vertical reference
official_sources.finding: The 1 m composite DTM covers about 99% of England, is distributed as GeoTIFF tiles aligned to the OS National Grid, uses metres and Ordnance Datum Newlyn with OSTN15, combines surveys from 2000-2022, and uses bilinear interpolation where resampling occurred.
official_sources.limitation: Composite age and resampling vary spatially; exact extrema need the contributing survey/tile lineage and should not assume native-sample equivalence after bilinear resampling.
official_sources.licence_or_attribution: Open Government Licence; Environment Agency attribution stated on dataset page

official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles — survey-specific raster archive
official_sources.finding: The timestamped DTM archive provides survey-specific raster elevation data at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m resolutions in 5 km GeoTIFF packages, aligned to the OS Grid, referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn, with a stated +/-15 cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
official_sources.limitation: Resolution and capture date vary by survey; the correct timestamped asset must be selected by the parcel location and metadata rather than by filename guess.
official_sources.licence_or_attribution: Environment Agency public dataset; dataset page identifies licence information

official_sources.title: Environment Agency National LIDAR Programme — 1m England coverage and survey-block phases
official_sources.finding: The National LIDAR Programme provides 1 m elevation data for all England, with 302 Phase-1 blocks captured between 2017 and 2023 and later repeat phases for selected blocks; the metadata catalogue exposes downloadable survey-block indexes.
official_sources.limitation: A national programme block does not by itself identify which survey or phase contributes the exact target pixel; the parcel must be intersected with current survey metadata.
official_sources.licence_or_attribution: Open Government Licence; Environment Agency attribution stated on dataset page

official_sources.title: Ordnance Survey coordinate transformations — OSTN15/OSGM15 and ODN
official_sources.finding: OS states that GNSS positions are referenced to ETRS89, OS mapping uses OSGB36 National Grid and mean-sea-level datums such as ODN, and OSTN15/OSGM15 link GNSS 3D positions to the national horizontal and height reference systems.
official_sources.limitation: Correct model naming is not enough; execution must preserve source/target CRS, model version, units and transformation provenance for each elevation.
official_sources.licence_or_attribution: Ordnance Survey public technical documentation; OS website terms apply

official_sources.title: Ordnance Survey accuracy of OS Net, OSTN15 and OSGM15
official_sources.finding: OS reports OS Net station standard errors generally better than 0.008 m in plan and 0.020 m in height, and OSGM15 standard error in height of 0.008 m for Great Britain, while noting these transformation/model errors exclude GNSS heighting errors.
official_sources.limitation: Transformation/model error is only one uncertainty component and must not be added or substituted for LIDAR, sampling, geometry or temporal errors without an explicit error model.
official_sources.licence_or_attribution: Ordnance Survey public technical documentation; OS website terms apply

official_sources.title: OS Terrain 5 — resolution and typical terrain-model accuracy comparator
official_sources.finding: OS Terrain 5 is a photogrammetric terrain model with 5 m post spacing and a published typical accuracy level around the metre scale (product page states greater than 2 m RMSE), intended for regional landscape modelling rather than centimetre-level LIDAR validation.
official_sources.limitation: The wording on the product page is not a parcel-specific error guarantee; this source is used only to prevent treating a coarser photogrammetric product as an equivalent substitute for EA 1 m LIDAR.
official_sources.licence_or_attribution: Ordnance Survey product documentation; OS website/product licence terms apply
